than individual interventions and may support the weakest readers most effectively (Foorman & Torgesen, 2001; NRP, 2000; Nind et al.,
2004). The role of social processes as a tool for learning identiﬁed by Vygotsky (Palincsar, 1989) stresses that social group learning and

of reading interventions for children of 5–12 years of age show that interventions enabling group interactions reveal the strongest student
outcomes. The opportunity to interact with peers through group interventions also appears to result in positive social outcomes (Wanzek
et al., 2006). More generally, a review of small group learning with technology (Lou, Abrami, & d’Apollonia, 2001) found that across subject
areas and grade levels learning together related to higher achievement than learning alone.

In Study 1, Italy's cognitive map showed a remarkable rotation of
26.74 that shifted the longitudinal axis toward verticality, even if a
small oblique orientation was retained by the great majority of
participants. On average, in sketch maps the longitudinal axis angle
departed from the vertical axis by 16.18, a much lower value than
the actual rotation of 42.92. Previous literature showed that peo-
ple tend to localize geographical units hierarchically and relatively,
anchoring the positioning in a top-down process, starting from the
larger geographic units to more reﬁned and small ones (Stevens &
Coupe, 1978). Consistently with previous literature, our studies
conﬁrmed the validity of this part-whole heuristic.
In the ﬁrst study, Italy's rotation along the longitudinal axis had
relevant consequences on latitude and longitude estimations. In
60% of the latitude comparisons and 45% of the longitude com-
parisons for city pairs, the responses were signiﬁcantly counter-
factual, leading to a wrong assignment. The latitude differential
range was 9e278 km, while the longitude differential range was
14e356 km, encompassing a remarkable interval of variation.

difference in latitude or longitude, but in many cases they were also
found for remarkable differences. For example, Foggia is 270 km
